<a class="skip" href="#main-content">Skip to content</a><header class="site-nav"><a class="brand" href="../index.html" aria-label="GLOBE home"><svg viewBox="0 0 40 40" fill="none" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="20" cy="20" r="17" stroke="#64d7ce"/><ellipse cx="20" cy="20" rx="8" ry="17" stroke="#64d7ce"/><path d="M3 20h34M6 12q14 7 28 0M6 28q14-7 28 0" stroke="#64d7ce"/></svg>GLOBE</a><button class="menu-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="main-nav">Menu</button><nav class="nav-links" id="main-nav" aria-label="Main navigation"><a href="../index.html">Home</a><a href="../pages/about.html" aria-current="page">About</a><a href="../pages/research.html">Research</a><a href="../pages/network.html">Network</a><a href="../pages/people.html">People</a><a href="../pages/monitoring.html">Monitoring</a><a href="../pages/resources.html">Resources</a><a href="../pages/news.html">News</a><a href="../pages/join.html">Join</a><a href="../pages/members.html" class="members">Members</a></nav></header><div id="main-content"><section class="page-intro"><p class="eyebrow">ABOUT GLOBE</p><h1>An initiative across oceans.</h1><p>GLOBE focuses on <i>Vibrio</i> dynamics during extreme El Niño events, within the wider context of marine microbial responses to a warming ocean.</p></section><section class="wrap prose"><h2>Scientific scope</h2><p>El Niño alters oceanographic conditions, with effects that vary among regions. GLOBE investigates whether these changing conditions favour the introduction and expansion of pathogenic <i>Vibrio</i> lineages, while examining changes in microbial community composition and functional potential.</p><p>The initial initiative includes 29 coastal sampling stations in 23 countries, across the Pacific, Atlantic and Indian oceans and the Mediterranean Sea. These figures describe the project scope; the public registry will document confirmed station metadata separately.</p><h2>Observations before and during El Niño</h2><p>The project description specifies monthly sampling, increasing to fortnightly sampling as the El Niño front arrives. Seawater microbes, phytoplankton and zooplankton are considered alongside environmental measurements. Metagenomic sequencing and analysis of <i>Vibrio</i> isolates support comparisons before and during the event.</p><h2>International identity</h2><p>GLOBE is an independent international scientific collaboration. Participating national networks, including the Italian Omics Observatory Network, contribute to the shared initiative.</p><h2>Coordination and participation</h2><p>Project coordinators, institutional affiliations, funding acknowledgements and partner contacts will be listed after confirmation. No names or affiliations have been inferred.</p></section></div><footer class="site-footer"><div><strong>GLOBE</strong><p><i>Vibrio</i> dynamics and ocean microbiome research.<br>International collaboration across a changing ocean.</p></div><p>Project scope: 29 coastal stations · 23 countries<br><a href="../pages/resources.html">Sources & resources</a> · <a href="../pages/privacy.html">Privacy & data use</a><br>Website release candidate · Project content pending coordinator approval</p></footer><script src="../assets/js/site.js"></script>
